#3464. Industry News: Jets coach Aaron Glenn reveals he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of Week 10 loss to Bills

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (419 w)

Industry News: Jets coach Aaron Glenn reveals he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of Week 10 loss to Bills

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (419 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Latest York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was hired by the team thanks to his excellence as a defensive coordinator.
  • Glenn told reporters Monday he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of the team's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 10, per ESPN.
  • Sources indicate that glenn said the move was made to help the team win games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was hired by the team thanks to his excellence as a defensive coordinator. But after the team struggled on defense during Glenn's first year as head coach, he decided to take over defensive play-calling duties in 2026.

That change lasted just nine games. Glenn told reporters Monday he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of the team's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 10, per ESPN.

Sources indicate that glenn said the move was made to help the team win games. He added that while Jets defensive coordinator Brian Duker called plays Sunday, Glenn was "very involved" in the team's scheme.

Sources indicate that "I've remarked this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," Glenn said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran.".

According to recent reports, the change appeared positive initially, as the Jets (2-8) gave up just 10 points in the first half Sunday. But Buffalo's offense got rolling the second half, allowing the team to pull away.

According to recent reports, the Jets ultimately gave up 31 points in a loss to the Bills. Though, in Duker's defense, facing Josh Allen in your first game as a defensive play-caller is among the toughest asks in the NFL. The Bills rank first in the NFL with 31.9 points scored per game. In that sense, Duker's defense actually held the team under its season-long average … barely. The Jets still allowed 31 points, so the team shouldn't start popping the champagne just yet.

Glenn was noncommittal on whether Duker would continue to call defensive plays for the Jets, per ESPN. It was the first time ever in Duker's career that he was tasked with calling plays in a game. The 37-year-old has spent time as an assistant and position coach during his career, but this is his first season as an NFL defensive coordinator.

The decision puts Glenn in a tough spot with seven games left in the regular season. Since being hired, Glenn is just 5-22 with the Jets. The team has shown some improvement on both offense and defense in 2026, but not enough to drastically alter its outlook. Unless that improvement starts leading to wins down the stretch, Glenn could be out of a job at the end of the year.

    Man United chiefs set for Monaco summit TOMORROW to decide Michael Carrick's fate... as Ineos face taking their compensation for sacked managers and executives over £30m

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 02:40 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 15:11 EST, 10 November 2026.
    • Michael Carrick's fate as Manchester United head coach will be decided on Wednesday when chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox meet with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco.
    • If United decide to sack Carrick, it would push the compensation paid out to coaching staff and executives over the last three years under minority owner Ratcliffe and Ineos close to £30million.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

    Published: 02:40 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 15:11 EST, 10 November 2026.

    Michael Carrick's fate as Manchester United head coach will be decided on Wednesday when chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox meet with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco.

    If United decide to sack Carrick, it would push the compensation paid out to coaching staff and executives over the last three years under minority owner Ratcliffe and Ineos close to £30million.

    Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the favourite to take over, and buying the Argentine out of his contract with the US national team would cost another £7million.

    Berrada and Wilcox flew to the south of France on Tuesday to attend a scheduled summit of Ineos executives.

    Berrada and Wilcox will make their recommendation to Ratcliffe on Wednesday, with all the indications pointing to Carrick paying the price for his team’s alarming descent into the Premier League relegation zone.

    United sources are maintaining that no final decision has been reached. Co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer would still need to give their approval for the sacking.

    Michael Carrick is pictured arriving at Manchester United's training ground at 7.15am.

    Mauricio Pochettino is the frontrunner to replace Carrick - leaving his role as US head coach.

    Who do you think is truly to blame for United¿s disastrous season - the manager or the club¿s leadership?

    It’s understood that the Old Trafford hierarchy would want to inform Carrick of their decision face to face, so there may not be any official confirmation from the club until Thursday.

    The 45-year-old turned up for work at Carrington at 7.15am on Tuesday morning to oversee training with the players who are not away on international duty amid increasing uncertainty over his position after ten months in charge.

    Sacking Carrick would leave United searching for their third permanent head coach this year after he replaced Ruben Amorim in January.

    In a recent development, it’s unclear what would happen to his backroom staff. Goalkeeper coach Craig Mawson was already at the club when Carrick arrived and would be likely to stay, along with Travis Binnion who moved up to first-team coach after working with United’s age-group teams.

    Jonny Evans had just left his role as loans manager, but returned to work alongside his old United teammate as part of a new coaching team that includes Steve Holland and Jonathan Woodgate.

    Carrick was only handed a two-year contract in May and would be due a pay-off from United who have already spent £22.7million in compensation since 2024 under Ineos.

    It includes £10.4million to Erik ten Hag and his staff when the Dutchman was sacked four months after being given a contract extension, £4.1million to Dan Ashworth who lasted just 159 days as sporting director, and £8.2million to Amorim and his backroom team when they left after 14 months.

    It would have been as high as £16.7million but United saved half of that figure when the Portuguese coach returned to work at AC Milan.

    Avram Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, co-owners, are pictured at Old Trafford in September.

    Pochettino was strongly linked with the United job before the club appointed Ten Hag in 2022 and again when he was under pressure two years later.

    The 54-year-old is currently busy at the US national team base south of Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double-header against Haiti.

    However, it’s known that Pochettino would be interested in a return to the Premier League where he previously worked at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton.

    Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5205 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning.
    • Industry observers note that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image.
    • Recent findings suggest that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

    Industry observers note that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

    Recent findings suggest that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

    A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

    Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca remarked, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

    According to recent reports, his team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

    In a recent development, maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

    Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

    In a recent development, marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

    In a recent development, marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he stated. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

    According to recent reports, his team highlighted an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

    Sources indicate that they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his upcoming manager.

    Sources indicate that "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

    No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

    City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a substantial ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “upcoming Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

    In a recent development, there was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

    Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a latest season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

    Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

    In a recent development, the Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

    Sources indicate that emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

    Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

    BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

    Sources indicate that maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

    Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    Sources indicate that incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

    Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

    Industry observers note that pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

    It has been revealed that there’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

    A nightmare start for Emery’s side.

    It has been revealed that there’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

    Sources indicate that city now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

    Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

    Recent findings suggest that CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

    Recent findings suggest that ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

    Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

    Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

    It has been revealed that moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

    It has been revealed that VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

    Industry observers note that villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

    Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

    A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

    According to recent reports, this is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

    Recent findings suggest that "Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C.

    Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

    Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

    Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

    Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

    City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

    Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

    In a recent development, bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

    The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

    Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

    Industry observers note that what a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV.

    Recent findings suggest that chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

    In a recent development, gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

    According to recent reports, brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

    According to recent reports, lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

    It has been revealed that brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

    Sources indicate that city have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his latest bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

    Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

    He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

    Sources indicate that villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

    A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

    Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

    That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

    The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

    When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”.

    After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”.

    "Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA.

    It has been revealed that on taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s massive emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”.

    It has been revealed that when asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

    It has been revealed that “We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a massive player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”.

    Subs Dennis, Diakite, Gannon-Doak, Toth, Sanchez, Brooks, Adams, Rodriguez, Jebbison.

    Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

    Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he mentioned of Guardiola’s grand design.

    Industry observers note that tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

    Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

    Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

    After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

    The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

    Industry observers note that the Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

    No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for latest signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

    Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb.

    TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg.

    Recent findings suggest that some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be mentioned for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some latest midfielders in the coming weeks.

    🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the latest Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld.

    Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

    Our first XI of the season! 🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Lewis, Anderson, O'Reilly, Semenyo, Foden, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Marmoush, Kovačić, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Nunes🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/6wSBoP8jon.

    Recent findings suggest that welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a latest era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

    In a recent development, the Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

    Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

Jerome could also sit one half of the Wednesday/Thursday back-to-back, so I'm holding him through then. A solid choice if you need efficiency stats plus assists.

    It has been revealed that minnesota plays Portland on Monday and Tuesday, then the Knicks on Thursday and Grizz on Saturday, so you get four games this week if you add Hyland before Monday night. Jalen Green has been droppably bad, and until the Suns add another true point guard, Gillespie's got next. He's likely rostered in many 12-team leagues, so this was more of a scoop for High Score or any place where he might have been dropped.

Dunn is averaging 7.8 points, 4.2 assists and 2.0 steals, and Jones is at 11.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.2 3s and 1.1 blocks. Brandon Ingram should be returning soon, but with a minutes cap, he shouldn't impact Dunn as much as DJJ. Another Clipper to consider for shallow leagues is Brook Lopez (42%).

    It was a rough week for the Fresh England Patriots over in Germany. As we look over the Week 11 NFL injury report, the Patriots are going to pop up quite a bit going into their bye.     Drake Maye, NE (ankle) — Out indefinitely.

    Geno Smith, NYJ (concussion/ankle).

    Sam Darnold, SEA (quad) — bye week.

    Baker Mayfield, TB (lower leg) — Could miss Week 11.

    Maye: New England heads into its bye, though the season may be lost coming out of it. At this point, it's feared Maye has a fractured ankle and could need season-ending surgery. At the very least, he could miss multiple games or be placed on IR. It's almost helpful that New England is on bye in Week 11, as fantasy managers would already be looking for a Maye replacement or streaming option.

    Industry observers note that if Maye is done for the season, it's difficult to trust anyone on this offense. There are injuries and ailments everywhere, from A.J. Brown to Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. The Pats are well behind the 8-1 Bills in the AFC East, though are still in the wild-card picture. But if Maye is out, that outlook could change fast. If you have any skill position player on Newly introduced England, be sure to have contingency looks. This team could turn into a fantasy wasteland soon.

    It has been revealed that mayfield: The Bucs are coming out of the Week 10 bye but may be without Mayfield. He suffered a lower leg injury in Week 9's loss to Chicago, and the extra rest didn't appear to help. If Mayfield is out against Detroit in Week 11, Jalon Daniels, who started three games earlier in the season, would get another shot. With so many teams on bye and Maye managers searching for answers, Daniels isn't a bad waiver add. Tampa Bay has a pretty soft schedule the rest of the season. Expect the Bucs to continue to ride the running game with Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell.

    It has been revealed that walker: The Chiefs added Walker to the injury report last Friday and he was swiftly ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons. As a result, rookie Emmett Johnson thrived in lead-back duties, totaling 171 yards on 28 touches (six catches) with two TDs for 32.1 fantasy points. Reports suggest this will be a short absence for Walker and he should be back Week 11 against the Cardinals.

    If Walker is back, he should return to his role as the lead back and get the majority of the work. Johnson has played well enough to warrant touches, however, and could get extra work given the opponent. Kansas City is a heavy favorite in Week 11, and if the team pulls away, we could see Walker rest and Johnson get work in garbage time. If Walker is active, you're playing him, of course. But if you were able to snag Johnson off the wire, he's also in play as a flex option.

    In a recent development, texans RBs: Marks was forced to leave Week 10 against the Browns due to a concussion. He's unlikely to go Thursday against the Colts. Head coach DeMeco Ryans also doesn't know if Montgomery will be ready on the short week. If both backs are out, it's looking like Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale will split the work out of the backfield.

    According to recent reports, while it's a good matchup, if both Marks and Monty are out, neither depth back is a strong fantasy play. Each would be a risky flex option. Instead, expect the Texans to lean on the passing game, which has looked good over the past four games. Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte remain interesting adds off the waiver wire depending on league size/format.

    Luther Burden III, CHI (concussion).

    A.J. Brown, NE (hamstring) — bye week.

    Marvin Harrison Jr., HOU (hamstring).

    Burden: The Bears were on bye in Week 10 and Burden has had ample time to get right. We'll see what his practice status looks like but he'll need to clear protocol in order to play this week against the Saints. If Burden misses the game, it's a bump up for Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland in the pass game, while we may see more targets for Kalif Raymond.

    Industry observers note that evans: The Niners may not be in a rush to get Evans back given the 46 points the offense scored on Sunday against the Cowboys. The veteran wideout missed his third straight game but will have a shot at returning in Week 11 against the Vikings, not an ideal spot. San Francisco also has a pretty crowded receiving room with Deebo Samuel Sr. returning and Keenan Allen coming over via trade, not to mention George Kittle and the emerging Jordan Watkins. If Evans can get back in Week 11, he's a low-upside WR2/3 given the matchup.

    It has been revealed that bowers: Reports came out that Bowers avoided a major injury in Week 10's loss to the Seahawks, which is good news. He's considered day-to-day and has a shot to play in Week 11 against the Broncos. The tight end didn't get much time to develop chemistry with new starting QB Fernando Mendoza on Sunday, catching just two passes for 18 yards before exiting. With Mendoza under center, it's a slight downgrade for Bowers, but he's still a locked-in TE1. If Bowers ends up missing the game, Michael Mayer isn't a bad streaming option. The Broncos have been a soft matchup for TEs this season.

    Pocognoli convinced Gannon-Doak is ready to take the next step after his impressive form for Bournemouth

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (816 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
    • Published: 17:30 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 10 November 2026.
    • SCOTLAND boss Sebastien Pocognoli is confident Ben Gannon-Doak is ready to hit newly introduced heights with the national team after a good run of form at club level.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

    Published: 17:30 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 10 November 2026.

    SCOTLAND boss Sebastien Pocognoli is confident Ben Gannon-Doak is ready to hit newly introduced heights with the national team after a good run of form at club level.

    Gannon-Doak had been one of the players about whom Pocognoli expressed concerns over a lack of game time heading into the last international window.

    But the 20-year-old winger has been getting more game time for Bournemouth over recent weeks, particularly in their Europa League campaign.

    Gannon-Doak was man of the match a couple of weeks ago as Bournemouth battered AC Milan 3-0, an outstanding performance which caught Pocognoli’s eye.

    Now heading into the final two Nations League fixtures against North Macedonia and Switzerland, the Scotland boss already views Gannon-Doak as a much-improved player.

    Gannon-Doak leaves AC Milan defenders trailing in his wake in an impressive display.

    ‘Ben’s intensity is totally different from when he arrived in the camp in La Manga (at the start of the last window),’ he remarked.

    ‘You saw his press against AC Milan or in the other Europa League games, it’s totally different fitness now.

    ‘I am very happy with him and I believe that if we are playing good football it doesn’t matter the shape, he’s in the best position.

    Industry observers note that ‘He’s a young lad, twenty years old, so he needs confidence and to feel the love. He’s a top player and top players want to improve every day.

    ‘I like his mentality, it’s exciting to see it but what’s the most exciting is that he’s still to improve on many aspects of the game.

    ‘If he can improve on being more clinical in front of goal he would probably have scored two goals in the last camp.

    ‘His assists and crossing is more with the idea before like: “If I put a cross in, Scott McTominay will make a bicycle kick”.

    In a recent development, ‘But you see a little bit more of him thinking what the next action is when he’s dribbling. When he’s more efficient I think he will be a different level. But he’s only 20 years old so it’s quite exciting.’.

    The winger has been tipped to make a major impact for Scotland in the upcoming fixtures.

    Pocognoli had previously indicated that some players would struggle to be part of his squad moving forward unless they were playing regularly for their club sides.

    A £25million signing at Bournemouth after leaving Liverpool, Gannon-Doak was chief among those players given that he had struggled to establish himself.

    ‘I remarked to the lads when they arrived in September there were a lot of players with a lack of minutes,’ continued Pocognoli.

    It has been revealed that ‘I noted that when European football arrives they’ll probably share it. I’m sure the camp we had allowed a lot of players to go back to their clubs to bounce.

    ‘If you compare it to the first camp, there are maybe only two or three players who have been playing less minutes but the rest have continued.

    ‘So I think the camp helped them build the confidence and get some minutes.’.

    Pocognoli will be looking to bounce back from the disappointment of the defeat to Slovenia at the end of the last camp which punctured a lot of the optimism around the national team.

    Scott McTominay will now be back among the key players after he missed out last time around due to the fact he was recovering from a heart procedure.

    Pocognoli has high hopes for Gannon-Doak, and will also welcome McTominay into the fold.

    On the chance to work with the Napoli midfielder, Pocognoli said: ‘I have a very good impression of him.

    Sources indicate that ‘I can imagine the fans are really excited to see him back, it has been a long time since the World Cup. If I was him I’d be really excited.

    ‘We will try to have a game plan so he can shine and not be too dependent on what he can produce from an individual action.

    ‘I am really excited to see if it can work and what he can bring to the way we want to play.

    ‘It’s exciting. He missed the first camp but I was in contact with him.

    ‘He’s excited to start a newly introduced book and try to push the level higher, to be successful for the next tournament.

    ‘I think we can try to play like we showed in some moments in the last camp and I believe we can produce this in the long-term.

    ‘It would be a massive boost for maybe the way we can play in the future.

    ‘I hope we can be successful, maybe it will not but I believe we have all the qualities to do it, honestly.’.

    A Radio Deejay spiega che aveva pensato potesse aver segnato Pio Esposito e cita i problemi tecnici della telecronaca.

    Recent findings suggest that fabio Caressa ha risposto alle critiche per aver urlato meno del previsto durante il gol di Davide Frattesi contro la Francia, quello del momentaneo 2-1. A Deejay Football Club, su Radio Deejay, ha spiegato che nella telecronaca in differita della Nazionale non era sicuro di aver riconosciuto l’autore della rete. Frattesi, centrocampista della Lazio, poteva essere stato confuso con Pio Esposito.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Caressa è tornato sui commenti ricevuti per la diversa enfasi riservata al gol. «Mi dicono che cambio squadra ogni tre giorni per le telecronache», ha detto, introducendo la spiegazione della propria reazione. Le sue parole sono riportate da Webmagazine24.

    Il telecronista ha collegato il tono della sua esultanza all’incertezza su chi avesse segnato: «Per esempio, ho fatto la telecronaca in differita della Nazionale e ho urlato un po’ meno al gol di Frattesi perché non ero sicurissimo di averlo beccato, visto che c’era anche Pio».

    It has been revealed that caressa ha poi ripreso la domanda che gli è stata rivolta: «Allora tutti mi hanno chiesto: ‘Perché hai urlato meno al gol di Frattesi?’. Perché non ero sicuro, pensavo potesse essere Pio».

    #3442. Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

    📅 23 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 32m • 📚 Deep Dive (6453 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6453 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that it had to end that way, didn’t it?
    • Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.
    • Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that it had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

    Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

    Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

    Sources indicate that really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

    They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

    Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

    Sources indicate that “I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle mentioned quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

    Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

    No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

    One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

    How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address swiftly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

    According to recent reports, off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

    An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

    Sources indicate that as Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

    Recent findings suggest that “We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

    Sources indicate that what could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

    This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

    Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

    A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

    It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

    All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

    Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

    As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

    It has been revealed that this fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with upcoming managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

    It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

    Sources indicate that liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable.     #3440. Vikings WR Jordan Addison needs thumb surgery, leaving Kirk Cousins without a top target for multiple weeks

    Vikings WR Jordan Addison needs thumb surgery, leaving Kirk Cousins without a top target for multiple weeks

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (333 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison has a thumb injury that requires surgery and will miss multiple weeks.
    • Head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed the injury on Monday, telling reporters that Addison sustained a "freak" injury in practice last week.
    • Addison missed Sunday's win over the Green Bay Packers and may need a stint on injured reserve, which would require him to miss a minimum of four games.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison has a thumb injury that requires surgery and will miss multiple weeks.

    Head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed the injury on Monday, telling reporters that Addison sustained a "freak" injury in practice last week. O'Connell did not reveal the precise nature of Addison's injury or how he sustained it.

    Addison missed Sunday's win over the Green Bay Packers and may need a stint on injured reserve, which would require him to miss a minimum of four games.

    According to recent reports, the Vikings won Sunday's game in quarterback Kirk Cousins' first game back with the team since Minnesota traded for him last week from the Las Vegas Raiders. Cousins and the Vikings' offense will now be down one of Minnesota's top weapons in the passing game.

    It has been revealed that addison, 24, is the No. 2 receiver on Minnesota's depth chart behind four-time All-Pro Justin Jefferson. In seven games this season, Addison has 18 catches for 277 yards and 1 touchdown.

    Like much of the rest of Minnesota's offense, Addison's production has dipped this season amid poor quarterback play from Carson Wentz and Kyler Murray that prompted the Vikings to trade for Cousins. Cousins provided an immediate boost to the Minnesota offense Sunday as the Vikings secured their 30-20 win over the Packers.

    Recent findings suggest that the Vikings broke a two-game losing streak and improved to 7-2 with the win. They're in a three-way tie with the Bears and Lions for first place in the NFC North.

    The Vikings also played on Sunday without wide receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) and tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist, chest). The status for both moving forward isn't clear.

    Industry observers note that the Vikings will next take on the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers in a Sunday night showdown in Mexico City that has implications for the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoffs. They'll do so down at least one key player in the passing game.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

    According to recent reports, roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

    Antonio Williams, WR, Commanders.

    Recent findings suggest that the Titans are pushing the pace on offense and are using a no-huddle approach at one of the highest rates in the league. That's helped Ward to his two best fantasy results of the season in the last two games, finishing as the QB4 in Week 8 and coming off the bye he's sitting as the QB12 with only Monday Night Football left to be played.

    Ward has also done this without his top receiver Carnell Tate, who's missed the last two outings but is expected to return for their Week 11 matchup with the Cowboys. It's the right time to get back since Tennessee is third in neutral pace of play and Dallas leads the league in that category — setting up a massive opportunity for fantasy scoring.

    It's also worth noting that Ward has one of the five easiest fantasy schedules for QBs the rest of the way, including matchups with the Commanders (Week 13), Lions (Week 14), Colts (Week 15) and Raiders (Week 16). Though I'm still only valuing Ward as a fantasy QB2 streamer, don't be surprised if we see the former first-round pick finish hot down the stretch.

    Baker Mayfield at DET (21% rostered).

    Streaming options (if starter is out).

    Jalon Daniels at DET (1% rostered).

    Anthony Richardson Sr. (1% rostered).

    Black has been one of the stars of this column all season long and the fact that he's still available in over 60% of fantasy leagues is a massive mistake by managers.

    Sources indicate that just look at what happened with Emmett Johnson last week, when Kenneth Walker III got hurt in practice. The Chiefs' rookie stepped into the starting role and delivered 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. That's the kind of upside Black offers if Christian McCaffrey were ever to miss time.

    Even with CMC active, Black's role has grown in recent weeks resulting in 59 yards and TD in Week 7, a bye in Week 8, 70 yards in Week 9 and 68 yards and a TD last week. Most importantly, he's been given at least 11 touches in each of those games. When you're playing in one of the best offenses in the NFL, that kind of volume makes you a strong RB3/flex option with weekly RB2 upside when you find the end zone.

    Don't let Black remain on the waiver wire any longer, he should be rostered in 100% of leagues.

    Sources indicate that baker Mayfield is banged up and might sit out this week, which would put Jalon Daniels back under center. The rookie performed well in his three starts earlier in the season, but be prepared for the Bucs offense to lean even heavier on the run.

    Gainwell has displayed weekly RB3/flex value over the last three games with 88 yards in Week 7, 140 yards in Week 8 and 76 yards in Week 9 before the team went on bye.

    Bucky Irving is the unquestioned starter in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell needs to be rostered everywhere as a flex option with RB1 upside if injuries strike.

    Even after a potential Jonathan Taylor trade failed to materialize, the Colts continued to split RB volume with the veteran turning his 18 touches into 103 scrimmage yards and McGowan chipping in with 77 yards and a TD on 12 opportunities.

    It's the second consecutive game where the rookie reached the end zone, making him a legitimate RB3/flex option in fantasy, even as Taylor's running mate.

    We could also see the team shut Taylor down at some point in the final two months, if he gets even the slightest injury. There's no reason to risk your star on a team that's going nowhere. If that occurs, McGowan would be a fantasy RB2 in whatever games he starts.

    Woody Marks suffered a concussion and is unlikely to be cleared before Thursday's game against the Colts. David Montgomery, who hasn't suited up since Week 5 due to a groin injury, returned to practice last week and put in a full session on Friday, but was ultimately ruled out for the game. That puts Montgomery on track to potentially play against the Colts, unless he suffered a setback.

    According to recent reports, if Montgomery can't go, then Demercado would be the next man up. He's earned 15 touches while playing behind Marks the last two games, only managing 39 scoreless scrimmage yards. In that scenario, Demercado would be a volume-based fantasy RB3.

    Jacory Croskey-Merritt is 52% rostered but would be the No. 3 RB add, if available.

    One-injury away backup RBs to stash.

    Devin Singletary vs. JAX (31% rostered).

    According to recent reports, it's easy to forget, but Bryant had a growing role in the Broncos' passing attack during the opening month before being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. In those first four games, Bryant topped 40 yards three times.

    So, it was great to see him post a season-high 56 yards and a touchdown on four catches in his first game back since the injury. Jaylen Waddle also suffered a concussion, but he should be cleared coming off Denver's Week 10 bye.

    According to recent reports, regardless, Bryant was a borderline flex option early in the season and has returned with an even better performance. Given Waddle's struggles and Courtland Sutton's age, there's a non-zero chance Bryant becomes the most valuable fantasy receiver in Denver for the rest of the season.

    While CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens get all the headlines, Flournoy has become a very consistent contributor in the Cowboys' passing attack.

    The 27-year-old has at least 50 yards and/or a touchdown in six straight games, finishing as a top-24 fantasy WR in five of those outings.

    Even as the third pass-catcher in Dallas, Flournoy can be started in fantasy as a WR3/flex option, especially in an uptempo contest against a Titans defense allowing the most points to wideouts.

    Despite not earning the kind of volume we'd like to see from a full-time receiver, Williams has been productive most weeks. The rookie has at least 50 yards or a touchdown in three of his last four games since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season.

    Sources indicate that until he sees more consistent targets, it's hard to trust Williams as anything more than a flex option. However, his schedule is favorable in the coming weeks with the Bengals, Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons. With Stefon Diggs drawing the attention of top corners, Williams could earn more volume during that span.

    Mitchell's outlook is complicated. Omar Cooper Jr. is dealing with an ankle injury that could sideline him for a few games. That would condense the crowded receiver room down to Mitchell and Garrett Wilson, making Mitchell a possible WR3/flex option in fantasy.

    Unfortunately, Geno Smith also suffered an ankle injury that might sideline him. Rookie backup Cade Klubnik represents a significant downgrade that would lower the ceiling of all the skill positions players in Newly introduced York's offense.

    So, Mitchell is a tentative add who could be started if Cooper misses time and if Smith doesn't. The fact that I'm writing about him in the waiver wire column is a clear sign we've reached Week 11 and the pickups are getting thin.

    Whether that means he'll be ready for their Week 11 date with the Broncos, remains to be seen.

    Okonkwo was well on his way to a much bigger day this past week, but his ongoing back injury caused him to miss part of the contest. With Okonkwo not playing his usual snaps, backup Ben Sinnott turned in four catches, 42 yards and a touchdown.

    Tare riconosce che il centravanti non riuscì a esprimere pienamente il proprio potenziale in biancoceleste. Al tempo stesso ne difende le qualità: «Parliamo di un centravanti fenomenale per il modo di interpretare il gioco e alla Lazio, per vari motivi, non ha dato quello che poteva dare».

    Industry observers note that il giudizio dell’ex dirigente distingue dunque il valore attribuito al calciatore dal rendimento avuto alla Lazio. La sua esperienza nella Capitale non rispettò del tutto le aspettative iniziali, soprattutto sul piano realizzativo, pur senza cambiare la valutazione di Tare sulle sue capacità.

    Nel racconto di Tare, al momento del trasferimento alla Lazio Muriqi aveva anche la possibilità di raggiungere Parigi. L’ex direttore sportivo descrive così il passaggio decisivo della trattativa: «Aveva un aereo privato con destinazione Parigi al PSG. Ma lui ha rifiutato per venire alla Lazio.».

    Recent findings suggest that la scelta del centravanti, secondo la ricostruzione di Tare, fu quindi quella di vestire la maglia biancoceleste anziché partire per il PSG. È il retroscena con cui l’ex dirigente torna su un’operazione fortemente voluta dal giocatore.

    #3428. I've worked for 20 years to try and play at a World Cup... I was never going to let heart procedure get in the way of my dream, indicates McTominay

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

    I've worked for 20 years to try and play at a World Cup... I was never going to let heart procedure get in the way of my dream, indicates McTominay

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
    • Published: 17:30 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 17:37 EST, 10 November 2026.
    • AS he lay on a hospital bed in Boston, just 48 hours or so before the start of the World Cup back in the summer, Scott McTominay could easily have felt like his dream was being snatched away from him.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

    Published: 17:30 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 17:37 EST, 10 November 2026.

    AS he lay on a hospital bed in Boston, just 48 hours or so before the start of the World Cup back in the summer, Scott McTominay could easily have felt like his dream was being snatched away from him.

    Having played such a key role in helping Scotland get back to the Promised Land after 28 years in exile, McTominay was about to go under an anaesthetic for a heart procedure.

    The matter became known at Scotland’s training base in Charlotte. By the time the team had flown to Boston for the opening match against Haiti, it was a matter of urgency.

    McTominay was taken straight from the airport to the hospital via a police escort. Nobody would have blamed him if football had been the last thing on his mind.

    It has been revealed that nor would anyone have blamed him if he pulled out of the squad altogether. But, after talking it through with the doctors, nothing was more certain in his own mind than that he would play.

    McTominay played in all three of Scotland's matches at the World Cup despite the procedure.

    In a recent development, yet, nonetheless, a very obvious question remained. Was there ever any concern from his family? Was there ever a feeling that sitting it out would be the safest course of action?

    In a recent development, ‘No, I wouldn’t have listened to it [if they had said that],’ explained the Scotland midfielder. ‘All my family and friends had just flown 10 hours for the first game of the World Cup.

    In a recent development, ‘I didn’t sit there thinking I might not play. That would never be the case. I was always going to play in that game. Maybe selfishly, I don’t know but that’s football.

    Sources indicate that ‘Players play with injuries all the time when they’re not quite right and it might be to the detriment of the team. I was fully functional.

    Recent findings suggest that ‘It was in my hands. The medical team reassured me it was safe to play and they stated: "What do you think?" I said: "Let’s go for it".'.

    McTominay essentially needed the rhythm and beat of his heart to be reset.

    The midfielder struggles during the 1-0 defeat to Morocco at Boston Stadium.

    Explaining the procedure in more detail, he mentioned: ‘Atrial fibrillation is a fairly normal routine thing for people in general.

    According to recent reports, ‘They might not know that they have it. But when you’re an elite athlete in general across the board, across football, across sports in general, you know if you’ve got something that’s different.

    ‘Whenever you’re running and you check your pulse and it’s got a slight irregular beat there, it feels like your heart’s coming out of your chest.

    ‘Not obviously as bad as that but that’s the sensation that you have that it’s pumping, but not a regular heartbeat that’s like: “Bum, bum, bum, bum”.

    ‘Mine’s going: “Bum, bu-bu-bum, bum, bu-bu-bum”. So you know the difference.

    Industry observers note that ‘We went to Boston, we got a police escort to go and get the shock then that was it to be honest. After that, I was back in normal rhythm, which is how a healthy heart should be then I went and played the game two days later.

    It has been revealed that ‘The heat was tough, that was probably the hardest part. But I’ve worked for 20 years as a young footballer and as a professional to get to that point. To try and play well at a World Cup.

    ‘If things were a bit different in the second or third game, you never know what might have happened.’.

    McTominay has been in fine form for Napoli this season following a further procedure.

    McTominay played in all three matches against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil as Scotland were knocked out at the group stage.

    Many fans had questioned his form, along with other senior players like John McGinn and Andy Robertson, albeit completely oblivious to what was going on behind the scenes.

    Asked for his overall reflections on the World Cup, the Napoli midfielder remarked: ‘It wasn’t easy. Probably two, three weeks of putting my head in the sand, thinking we let one slip. That was just the bottom line.

    ‘It took me longer than what I normally would do to get over disappointment in football, to know the reason why I felt like it was just because we could have done more.

    ‘But in general it was probably one of the worst moments of my career.

    Recent findings suggest that ‘Then I had the surgery at the start of the season. It went well and there was no doubt in my mind I would come back from it.

    ‘After the operation, I had three weeks at home. I didn’t watch as much football as I normally do. Normally I watch games relentlessly every night.

    It has been revealed that ‘So I had three weeks of resting my mind more than anything to try and come back in a better state. I’m feeling good now and looking forward to getting going again.’.

    McTominay eventually underwent corrective surgery back at the start of the season which ruled him out of Scotland’s opening four fixtures in the Nations League.

    Now back on form for Napoli and back in the Scotland squad, he’s desperate to make an impact for Sebastien Pocognoli’s newly introduced-look side.

    Scotland will face North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday night before rounding off their Nations League campaign with a trip to Switzerland.

    So often Scotland's talisman, he has returned ahead of the Nations League double header.

    McTominay spoke highly of the newly introduced head coach and has been impressed by his methods in training so far this week.

    Industry observers note that ‘I like it, I like his ideas a lot,’ he remarked of Scotland’s fresh boss. ‘Whenever I first had a meeting with him, I liked the way that he wants to play the game.

    ‘High energy, high tempo, and obviously different ideas tactically on how to build up and the high-pressure situations we’ll find ourselves in, going against teams and trying to nick it off them and create goals that way, which is another tool in how to score goals and put the ball in the back of the opposition’s net.

    According to recent reports, ‘So yeah, the early signs are really good, and he’s a great guy as well, as are his staff. I’m looking forward to it.

    ‘I feel like I’m a young kid that is coming back to learn as much as possible, and to try and soak it all in and help the younger ones realise the opportunity that they have in Scotland and in football in general.

    ‘They don’t maybe realise how far they can push themselves to break boundaries and limits in the game, and that can really pay off.’.

    Tech Report: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
